item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 represented chain A of 1acc as one domain, d1acca_. Later SCOPe revisions retired that whole-chain treatment and divided the chain into separately indexed N- and C-terminal domains, d1acca1 and d1acca2. This is a reannotation of domain boundaries, not a change in the experimental structure or proof that the two pieces have identical functions. It illustrates that an evolutionary domain is a reusable module: modules can be fused into one polypeptide, recombined independently, and have homologues with different neighboring domains. Homology searches should therefore query the two domain sequences separately and judge coverage against the revised boundaries; a hit to one domain supports ancestry only for that module, not automatically for the other domain or the full-length protein. Same-family matches provide the strongest basis for detailed transfer, same-superfamily membership supports more remote common ancestry but not unrestricted function transfer, and fold- or class-level similarity alone is insufficient evidence of homology. Templates and SCOPe representatives should likewise be selected per domain; a full-chain template is appropriate only when the complete architecture, linker, and inter-domain arrangement are also conserved.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
